name: Cloudbeds
description: Cloudbeds reservations become events on the main guest's profile: Cloudbeds Reservation Confirmed (once), Cloudbeds Reservation Cancelled and Cloudbeds Checked Out. Each reservation is also kept as a Cloudbeds reservation (its own type: status, dates, nights, guests, total, balance, and whether it's paid in full), checked again every hour for arrivals in the next week. Guests are held back from marketing: they booked, they didn't sign up. No revenue is recorded.

signature_secret.label: Webhook header value
signature_secret.help: A long random value you choose, for example the output of: openssl rand -hex 24. Give it as authHeaderValue (with authHeaderName X-Webhook-Token) when you create each Cloudbeds webhook.

credentials.name: api_key
credentials.label: Cloudbeds API key
credentials.help: An API key with the read:reservation scope (Cloudbeds → Account → Apps & Marketplace → API credentials). Used to fetch each reservation a webhook names and for the hourly payment check.

setup: Create the integration from this recipe and copy its webhook URL.
In Cloudbeds, create an API key with the read:reservation scope and save it as the credential api_key.

Pick a long random value and save it as the integration's signing secret. Cloudbeds doesn't sign webhooks (their timestamp isn't signed either); it sends this value in a header instead, and every webhook only names a reservation that DumbMail then fetches.

Create four webhooks with Cloudbeds' API: POST https://api.cloudbeds.com/api/v1.3/postWebhook (form fields) with object=reservation, action=created, endpointUrl=<webhook URL>, authHeaderName=X-Webhook-Token and authHeaderValue=<the same value>. Repeat with action=status_changed, action=dates_changed and action=deleted. Add ?propertyID=<id> to the address if your key covers several properties.
If the key covers several properties and this integration is for one of them, set property_id in the settings; reservations for other properties are ignored.
Make a test reservation and check the delivery log: each webhook is followed by a fetch of the reservation.

Every hour, DumbMail lists confirmed reservations arriving in the next payment_check_days days (7 by default) and fetches each one again: a payment changes the reservation's balance but sends no reservation webhook. Paid in full means Cloudbeds reports a balance of exactly zero and payments equal to the total.

Reservations are kept as their own type, Cloudbeds reservation, so flows built for other booking systems never act on them. This recipe ships no pre-arrival email: build one on Cloudbeds reservations yourself if you want it, and never put door codes or other access details in it.
No revenue is recorded. Cloudbeds reports money it has taken as posted transactions (its accounting/transaction webhook), which this recipe doesn't read.
Guests are held back from marketing. Guest documents, addresses, cards, notes and custom fields are never stored: only the fields the recipe reads are kept from each answer.
